items.claim: The front-seam warrant is contradicted by the bytes the row itself quotes: third-person description already runs in the immediately preceding verse and the row's opening word is a consecutive form binding it to that clause, and the parashah seg called the opening mark sits at the wrong seam.
items.evidence: Seam warrant: the edge is grounded on a turn to third-person description beginning at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3, but the second half of the immediately preceding verse is already third-person plural description of the same subject: כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים (oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, byte tier). Cross-seam continuity, undisclosed: the row's own opening splice begins וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ (oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3, byte tier), pointed vav plus patah followed by a dagesh-doubled yod, the consecutive prefix pattern, which continues the preceding clause rather than opening a fresh one. A byte-true continuity straddling the row's own front seam argues against the cut unless disclosed, and it is not disclosed. Mark position: WLC parashah segs are recorded against the verse they follow, so the seg at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 falls after the span's OPENING verse, inside the row, not at its front seam; oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, the verse immediately before the span, carries no seg at all (inventory: 0 segs at that MT key, single-witness, tier-3). The closing member of the pair, at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, is correctly placed. Verified clean and not challenged: both Hebrew splices reach byte tier at their cited MT keys; all four dual-cites are arithmetically right and land on the right MT content across the offset zone; span seg symmetry is complete (segs at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 and oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, 2 segs across the span's MT keys, both disclosed, SAMEKH and PE kept distinct); the closing נְאֻם יְהוָֽה at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 (byte tier) is present as claimed and is followed by a fresh formula onset; and the rejected-alternative observation that the two preceding wish-cries share one interrogative wish shape is byte-true at oshb:Jer.8.23 = web:Jer.9.1 and oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, though asserted without quoting either form.

items.claim: Both edges of the seam warrant lean on translation poetry-line layout, which is not evidence from either witness, while the Hebrew that would actually carry the prose-register claim is left unquoted.
items.evidence: The opening warrant places the interrogative in prose where the oracles on either side run in poetry, the closing warrant reads that the next verse returns to poetry, and the device notes repeat it. The underlying layout fact is true of the translation (zero poetry lines across web:Jer.9.12 = oshb:Jer.9.11 through web:Jer.9.16 = oshb:Jer.9.15, against three at web:Jer.9.11 = oshb:Jer.9.10 and two at web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16), but modern poetry-line breaks are translation layout rather than a signal of either witness, and the claim is translation-dependent in a further sense: the staged MT extract has no layout layer at all, so no Hebrew signal underwrites the register contrast. The Hebrew that would have carried it is unquoted: the prose consecutive forms וַיֹּ֣אמֶר (oshb:Jer.9.12 = web:Jer.9.13, byte tier) and וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ (oshb:Jer.9.13 = web:Jer.9.14, byte tier) open two of the span's five verses, and the relative particle recurs three times inside it. Verified clean: all three splices reach byte tier at their cited MT keys; the dual-cites are arithmetically right and content-correct across the offset zone (7 of 7); seg disclosure is complete for the span (3 segs across its MT keys) and correctly typed, the petuchah at oshb:Jer.9.15 = web:Jer.9.16 kept distinct from the setumot at oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12 and oshb:Jer.9.13 = web:Jer.9.14 (single-witness, tier-3). The decision NOT to cut at לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י (oshb:Jer.9.14 = web:Jer.9.15, byte tier) is byte-defensible even though the differentiator is not named: the comparable earlier onset at oshb:Jer.9.6 = web:Jer.9.7 follows the נְאֻם יְהוָֽה closure of oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 (byte tier), while oshb:Jer.9.13 = web:Jer.9.14 carries none.

items.claim: The addressee analysis is byte-wrong at the row's opening, the summons imperatives being plural forms addressed to the summoners rather than to the mourning women, and the transliteration erases the feminine-plural morpheme that actually marks the turn to the women.
items.evidence: At oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17 the imperatives are הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ (byte tier), both ending in the plural vav with dagesh and addressed to those told to summon; the women appear in that same verse, oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, as the object לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת and as the subject of the feminine-plural וּתְבוֹאֶ֑ינָה (byte tier). The turn to the women themselves comes at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20, with שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ and וְלַמֵּ֤דְנָה (byte tier), forms ending nun plus qamats plus he, the feminine-plural imperative ending. The rejected-alternative sentence assigns the whole preceding stretch to the women, which the bytes do not support for its first three verses, and the transliteration of שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20 is given without that ending, dropping exactly the morpheme that carries the feminine-plural addressee the argument depends on. Second defect, gloss extent against splice extent: the closing splice runs through כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל (oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, byte tier) while its gloss stops at the dung noun, leaving the following preposition spliced but unglossed. Verified clean and creditable: the variant-formula disclosure is exact and correctly kept out of the divine-speech census. The consonantal run koh neum YHWH occurs in exactly one verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, and that verse is absent from the koh amar YHWH set (sweep: 152 verses, skeleton tier). דַּבֵּ֗ר (oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, byte tier) is a singular imperative as claimed. Both seams are byte-strong and seg disclosure is complete and correctly typed for the span: PE at oshb:Jer.9.15 = web:Jer.9.16 immediately before, and the 2 segs across the span's MT keys both disclosed, SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.18 = web:Jer.9.19 and SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22 (single-witness, tier-3).

items.claim: The cross-reference propping the opening warrant is an untiered recurrence claim carrying no sweep digit, and the two sites are not the same shape in the bytes, differing precisely in the verse-initial property the warrant rests on.
items.evidence: The opener is הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25, byte tier), verse-initial. The site called the same shape reads לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32, byte tier): there the formula is prefixed by the therefore-particle and is not verse-initial, so the two differ exactly in the feature the seam warrant depends on, and the Hebrew is quoted at only one of the two sites. No tier is named on the recurrence claim and no digit accompanies it. The consonantal run occurs in 15 verses book-wide (sweep: 15 verses, skeleton tier), two of them within this stretch of the book, so it is a dense formula rather than a distinguishing onset marker, which the row does not say. Verified clean: both splices reach byte tier at their cited MT keys; the nation roster and the closing verdict both land on oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26 as cited; the refs check out at 4 of 4, the 3 that touch the offset zone all dual-cited and arithmetically right; the span carries 1 internal seg across its MT keys, the closing one at oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26 and the preceding seg at oshb:Jer.9.23 = web:Jer.9.24 is also disclosed (single-witness, tier-3), so seg symmetry is complete; and the disclosure separating this nation list from the header-bounded nations material later in the book is byte-appropriate, the list here being governed by a preposition chain within one verse, and carrying neither of the header shapes that bound the later nations material (inventory: 10 header sites, 6 lamed-initial and 4 non-lamed).

items.claim: The no-internal-seam warrant is falsified by the bytes the row itself quotes, a sustained singular address to Yahweh interrupting the plural addressees; the same warrant assigns the whole span to one speaker's mouth that the bytes contradict; and the Aramaic island's opening verb is mislabelled an imperative.
items.evidence: Stated warrant: nothing further in the span interrupts it, neither a divine-speech formula, an addressee shift, nor a discourse imperative. The formula half is byte-true (sweep: 2 verses carrying the consonantal run koh amar YHWH in MT chapter 10, at oshb:Jer.10.2 and oshb:Jer.10.18, the in-span occurrence being oshb:Jer.10.2). The addressee half is not. The addressees at oshb:Jer.10.2 and oshb:Jer.10.5 are plural, אַל תִּלְמָ֔דוּ and אַל תִּֽירְא֤וּ (byte tier), while the verse the row itself quotes turns to a sustained singular address to Yahweh: כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ (oshb:Jer.10.6, byte tier), carrying a second-person masculine singular suffix, the independent singular pronoun pointed alef-patah, tav-dagesh-qamats, he, and a second singular suffix on the name-noun, continued at oshb:Jer.10.7 with יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ and לְךָ֖ (byte tier). By the row's own stated criterion that is an addressee shift inside the span, and the row asserts its non-occurrence. Frame ownership: the surrounding mockery is placed in Yahweh's own mouth on the strength of the onset formula, but second-person praise addressed to Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.6 and oshb:Jer.10.7, and third-person predication about Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.10, וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (byte tier), cannot be that same speaker's; one formula-owner is asserted over material the bytes show carries 2 distinct speaker positions. Form class: the Aramaic island's opening verb is called a citation imperative, but כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11, byte tier, Aramaic) carries a tav prefix with dagesh and tsere and a final paragogic nun, a prefix-conjugation form rather than an imperative, and both witnesses render it as a modal future. No morphology layer is staged, so the label stands or falls on the pointed bytes plus the two renderings, and neither supports it; the same sentence also concedes a citation imperative immediately after asserting that no discourse imperative interrupts the span. Verified clean: the Aramaic island is disclosed as required, labelled Aramaic at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 and at no other coordinate (inventory: 15 Aramaic-coded morphs, all 15 in that one verse); the preceding seg is dual-cited correctly across the offset zone as web:Jer.9.26 = oshb:Jer.9.25 and the 3 segs across the span's MT keys are all disclosed (oshb:Jer.10.5, oshb:Jer.10.10, oshb:Jer.10.11, single-witness, tier-3), so seg symmetry is complete; all four splices reach byte tier at their cited keys; and the opening שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte tier) is a plural imperative as claimed.

items.claim: The twin cross-reference is an untiered recurrence claim that the consonantal evidence bears in part, and the ketiv/qere note is argued from an English rendering that cannot register the variant.
items.evidence: Twin claim: the narrow part is exact. יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ closes oshb:Jer.10.16 and יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ closes oshb:Jer.51.19, and the two runs are byte-identical. The wider designation is not. Of the five verse pairs, oshb:Jer.10.12 against oshb:Jer.51.15 and oshb:Jer.10.15 against oshb:Jer.51.18 are byte-identical, but the other three diverge already at skeleton tier: oshb:Jer.10.13 carries the ketiv/qere doublet מִקְצֵ֣ה ארץ הָאָ֑רֶץ where oshb:Jer.51.16 has the single מִקְצֵה אָ֑רֶץ, besides two divergent verb forms; oshb:Jer.10.14 carries the plene spelling of the refiner noun against the defective spelling at oshb:Jer.51.17; and oshb:Jer.10.16 has יַעֲקֹ֗ב with וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֵׁ֖בֶט against the plene יַעֲק֗וֹב with וְשֵׁ֖בֶט and no Israel noun at oshb:Jer.51.19. No tier is named anywhere on the recurrence claim, so which of these is being asserted cannot be read off it. Ketiv/qere: the note count at oshb:Jer.10.13 is inventory-true and both quoted forms are byte-true at that key. The supporting inference is not: that the qere supplies the definite reading carried into the English is translation-dependent, and the witnesses falsify it. The parallel verse carries the article-less מִקְצֵה אָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Jer.51.16, byte tier) and the translation renders it identically, “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.51.16), so the English cannot register the article and is not evidence for either reading. Verified clean: the participial opening עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ is verse-initial at oshb:Jer.10.12 (byte tier) and the closing name-formula is verse-final at oshb:Jer.10.16 (byte tier), so both edges carry byte warrants; the segs at oshb:Jer.10.11 (front seam) and oshb:Jer.10.16 (close) are inventory-true and correctly typed, the latter being the span's 1 internal seg across its MT keys, so seg symmetry is complete (single-witness, tier-3); no Aramaic label is applied to any verse of this span, and the neighbouring island verse is referred to at its own coordinate.
